origins.section: Equivalent Annual Cost Compares Options With Different Lives
Lifecycle Cost Is Every Cost of Owning the Asset, Discounted to One Date
Equivalent Annual Cost Assumes the Option Is Repeated Like for Like

recorded.prompt:q-eac-value: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-eac-value: EAC = LCC / a(r, L); output '1000 / annuity factor 94.39' at 7% over 20 years.
recorded.prompt:q-unequal-lives: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-unequal-lives: 'That comparison is wrong... The repair's $1,343k buys ten years of service; the replacement's $2,381k buys forty. The two numbers are not costs of the same thing.'
recorded.prompt:q-no-repeat: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-no-repeat: 'When the assumption fails, build the actual sequence of decisions over a common horizon and compare present values directly.'

recorded.prompt:q-eac-value:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-eac-value:a: 'Do not shortcut EAC to LCC/L... The divisor is the annuity factor, not the number of years.'
recorded.prompt:q-eac-value:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-eac-value:b: EAC = LCC x r/(1-(1+r)^-L), not LCC x r; LCC x r is the perpetuity case, and the page's figure is 94.39.
recorded.prompt:q-eac-value:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-eac-value:c: EAC is 'a level yearly payment over its own life', i.e. LCC / a(r, L), not LCC itself.
recorded.prompt:q-unequal-lives:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-unequal-lives:a: 'That comparison is wrong, and it is the most common mistake with lifecycle costs.'
recorded.prompt:q-unequal-lives:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-unequal-lives:c: 'Do not shortcut EAC to LCC/L. Dividing by the life ignores the time value of the money.'
recorded.prompt:q-unequal-lives:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-unequal-lives:d: Under EAC each repeat costs what the first did ('at the same real cost'), not nothing; also LCCs of different lives 'are not comparable'.
recorded.prompt:q-no-repeat:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-no-repeat:a: 'The shortcut carries the chain's assumption': EAC assumes like-for-like repeats, which here fails.
recorded.prompt:q-no-repeat:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-no-repeat:b: Same passage: when the repeat assumption fails, compare present values over a common horizon instead.
